rationale: This sample is a floating-point compute kernel (flops-8 plus math-benchmark sources) whose entire footprint is two tiny functions dominated by a hot arithmetic loop, so the priority is defending the loop body while keeping overhead low: RuntimeCost weights are the highest dimension for BCF and FLA (0.95) because bogus control flow and dispatch-loop flattening multiply per-iteration cost exactly where this program spends all its time, and their CorrectnessRisk/SizeCost weights are high so they are applied only where features strongly justify them; SUB gets a high CorrectnessRisk weight (0.9) since naive instruction substitution on FP arithmetic can change semantics, but a moderate security/diversity pull so it still applies where integer/logic ops appear; SPLIT is cheap, safe, and composes with other passes so its weights stay low across cost dimensions, letting it fire broadly; IBR keeps a moderate security pull with a raised RuntimeCost weight since indirect branching on a single tight loop adds measurable cost for little gain; ICALL is included with modest weights because this code has almost no call sites, so it contributes little either way; IGV is omitted entirely because the binary has essentially no global variable surface (810 total text bytes, no data-heavy globals) to protect, making the pass pure risk with no payoff.
